title: Sus & Diminished Chords
description: Two chords that build tension: suspended chords, which hang in the air, and diminished chords, which badly want to resolve.

steps.title: Beyond major and minor
steps.description:
Suspended (sus) chords swap out the third for a different note. With no third, the chord is neither major nor minor, so it seems to hang there, waiting:

• Sus4: the third moves up to the fourth
• Sus2: the third moves down to the second

Diminished chords stack two minor thirds. The result is tense and unstable, and it really wants to go somewhere.

steps.title: Play Csus4
steps.description: Play C, F and G. It's C major with F in place of E. Listen to how unfinished it feels, like it wants to settle back down.
steps.hint: Start from a C major shape (C, E, G), then slide your middle finger from E up one white key to F.

steps.title: Let it settle
steps.description: Now play C major (C, E, G). The F drops down to E, and the tension lets go.
steps.hint: Move your middle finger from F back down to E.

steps.title: Play Csus2
steps.description: Play C, D and G. This time the E drops down to D. Sus2 sounds open and airy, and you'll hear it a lot in rock and pop.
steps.hint: Thumb on C, index finger on D, pinky on G.

steps.title: Play B diminished
steps.description: Play B, D and F. That's a diminished triad. It sounds tense and uneasy, like something is about to happen.
steps.hint: All white keys. Each note is three half steps above the one before it.

steps.title: Resolve to C
steps.description: Now play C major. In the key of C, B diminished leans right into it: the B wants to step up to C, and the F wants to fall to E.
steps.hint: C, E, G. Notice how little your hand has to move to get there.

steps.title: What's suspended?
steps.description: In a sus4 chord, which note takes the place of the third?
